clue.text: Young dog, hard at work when rodent emerges

definitions.note: a clause describing the day rather than a noun; the answer names that day

indicators.note: letters that are at work are busy moving about, so the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puppy works hard while some burrowing animal pops out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: This puzzle, published on 2 February, has four different clues to GROUNDHOG DAY, echoing the film where the same day repeats.
explanation.definitionFit: On 2 February in North America, tradition watches a groundhog leave its burrow to forecast whether spring is coming early.

clue.text: Cooks topless — and burns
Yet another hit: youngster displacing top two

indicators.note: the first two letters are pushed out of the leading position and sent to the end

parts.note: a thump is a heavy blow
a teen is a young person

explanation.surface: A pop single is yet another hit, with a teenage star pushing the top two acts aside.
explanation.walkthrough: THUMP plus TEEN gives THUMPTEEN; moving its first two letters to the end gives UMPTEENTH.
explanation.definitionFit: The umpteenth time is one more in a long, tiresome series, hence yet another.

clue.text: Very late

definitions.meaning: second meaning: deceased, as in the late king

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'extremely tardy'; instead the two words are separate senses of one adjective-adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word is an intensifier meaning completely, and it also describes someone no longer alive.

clue.text: Work permit breaking record, public note

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: one word breaks into another, sitting inside it

parts.note: to enter details is to record them

explanation.surface: A work permit that breaks the record gets a public notice.
explanation.definitionFit: An open letter is addressed to someone but published for everyone to read, so it is a note made public.

clue.text: Information poster put up by corporation

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a corporation is a jocular old word for a large belly, or tum

explanation.surface: A company puts up an informative poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is not a company here: in British slang it means a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information or fact.

clue.text: Beatles song from Before Midnight?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1965 Paul McCartney ballad

definitions.note: a time phrase standing for the day just gone
definitions.meaning: second meaning: once midnight passes, everything before it belongs to the previous day

explanation.walkthrough: Before Midnight is a 2013 film, so the clue poses as asking which song features in it; read literally, it is the time before midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: The song is famous by that title, and the day that ended at the last midnight is the one before today.

clue.text: Land ho! Welcome to Australia, the source of many fresh starts

definitions.text: the source of many fresh starts

explanation.surface: A sailor sights land and is greeted on arrival in Australia, a place of new beginnings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests emigration to Australia; the definition is the 1993 film in which one day restarts again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: In the film, Bill Murray's weatherman wakes to the same morning over and over, so the day gives countless restarts.

clue.text: Doctor hiding antique behind coat

indicators.note: something hidden is tucked inside whatever hides it

explanation.surface: A doctor conceals a valuable antique behind his coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coat' looks like a garment, but it is the verb at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To gold-plate is to cover a metal object with a thin layer of gold, i.e. to coat it.

clue.text: Hound Dog adapted into American black and white movie

indicators.note: one part goes into another, sitting inside it

parts.note: grey, the mix of black and white, spelt the American way

indicators.note: a song adapted for the screen is reworked, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An Elvis hit adapted into an old monochrome American film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black and white movie' suggests an old film, but black and white together make the colour inserted round the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundhog Day is the 1993 comedy film starring Bill Murray.

clue.text: Weapon that a sergeant wields

indicators.note: the phrase holds the word in its grip, carrying it inside

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word, all of the next, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Asking what a police sergeant carries on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electroshock weapon that stuns by firing barbs on wires.

clue.text: Tory's struggling to eat English seafood

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one part goes within the other
someone struggling is in disarray, so these letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician is finding English seafood hard to swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is a shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: For the most part, full beam replaced with a torch

indicators.note: most but not all of the next word is kept, so its last letter goes
letters that are replaced are put back in different positions

parts.note: the word with its final letter cut

explanation.surface: A driver mostly has headlights on full beam, but swaps them for a flashlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full beam' pairs naturally with 'torch', but the torch is the definition and the beam is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, especially one made of several thick wicks.

clue.text: Man now coming with cash to pole dance

parts.note: King Charles III's portrait now appears on British coins and notes
north, one of the earth's poles

explanation.surface: A man arrives with money for a pole dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole dance' looks like one phrase, but it splits: pole is a letter and dance is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s jazz dance named after the city in South Carolina.

clue.text: Anyone leaving A&E without left stocking?

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, the remaining letters sit around another
letters that leave a word are removed from it

parts.note: these two letters are the ones removed

explanation.surface: Did anyone leave the hospital emergency department without the left one of a pair of stockings?
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital casualty department. The question mark marks the definition as a loose one: stockings are often called nylons.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings made from the synthetic fibre, so a single stocking can be called a nylon.

clue.text: One-time striker apparently losing weight without drug

indicators.note: being without something means lacking it, so it is taken out

explanation.surface: A former footballer seems to be slimming down without taking any drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer; it refers to the proverb that lightning never strikes the same place twice, hence 'apparently'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying holds that a bolt never hits the same spot twice, so it is something that supposedly strikes only once.

clue.text: Was gardener protecting daughter after nasty heat rash?

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one part goes inside another

parts.note: used a hoe, as a gardener does

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in sequence
something nasty has turned bad, so the next word's letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A gardener tended to a daughter after she broke out in prickly heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat rash' looks like one ailment; the definition is 'rash' alone, as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash person acts impulsively without thinking, which is what being hotheaded means.

clue.text: Festival gift perhaps wrapped around daisy, say

indicators.note: wrapping goes round the outside of a thing, so it ends up enclosed

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A spring present wrapped in paper with a daisy tied round it.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'perhaps' and 'say' give the same abbreviation for 'for example'; the first splits around the flower, the second follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate eggs are the traditional present exchanged at the Christian spring festival.

clue.text: Where one feels superior, drugged by heroin

explanation.surface: Someone feels above everyone else because heroin has got them stoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on their high horse is behaving arrogantly, assuming a superior moral position.

clue.text: Is mum giving permission?

wordplay.note: keeping mum means saying nothing; read as says plus the letter O for zero

explanation.surface: Asking whether a mother is granting permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother; it means silent, and someone silent says nothing, i.e. O.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their authorisation or approval for an action.

clue.text: Collected articles penned by Greek journalist

indicators.note: something penned by a word is fenced in by it, so it sits inside

parts.note: the indefinite and definite articles, a and the

explanation.surface: Someone gathered newspaper articles written by a Greek reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles penned by' suggests writing; the articles are grammatical ones and 'penned' means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have gathered things is to have collected them together.

clue.text: Muse's Origin of Symmetry missing from a store after renovation

indicators.note: a renovated building is rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged
a letter missing from a phrase is taken out of it
the origin is where the word begins, its opening letter

explanation.surface: The rock band Muse's album Origin of Symmetry is missing from a refitted record shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Muse are a British band and Origin of Symmetry is their 2001 album; here 'Muse' is the definition and the album title supplies wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Looked resentful in broadcast

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard rather than read, so the word goes by its sound

explanation.surface: Someone appeared bitter on a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looked resentful' reads as one phrase; 'Looked' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To peek is to take a quick, furtive look, so peeked means glanced.

clue.text: Australian native and Asian native visiting a king from the south

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside the place being visited
in a down clue, reading from the south means bottom to top

parts.note: a Lao is a person from Laos

explanation.surface: A native Australian and someone from Asia call on a monarch coming up from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is a tree-dwelling marsupial found only in Australia.

clue.text: Fish heart spurned by talk show host

indicators.note: the centre of the name is rejected and removed

parts.note: Oprah Winfrey, the American chat show host

explanation.surface: A fish's affections are rejected by a television presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: The opah, or moonfish, is a large, brightly coloured ocean fish.

clue.text: Inner self revealed in revolutionary examination

indicators.note: a revolution turns things around, so the letters read backwards
what is revealed inside a word was sitting within it all along

parts.note: the letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: One's true self is exposed under radical psychological scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology the anima is the inner personality or soul, as opposed to the persona shown to the world.

clue.text: Who might give ten percent a year to keep Republican in faraway town?

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

parts.note: someone leaving a gratuity of a tenth

explanation.surface: Who would hand over a tenth each year to support a Republican in some distant town?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the definition: the old song says it's a long way to Tipperary, a town in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipperary is an Irish town made famous as distant by the First World War marching song.

clue.text: Fat pig died in lively annual celebration

indicators.note: the preceding pieces sit inside the word that follows

parts.note: gay in its older sense of merry

explanation.surface: A fat pig expired in the middle of a lively yearly festival.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundhog weather tradition falls each year on 2 February, a recurring holiday.
